text:
alex (customer): Hey, we're seeing a weird resume behavior on streaming reads. Client disconnects -> reconnect with resume token, but the resumed stream sometimes emits an early EOF and a short duplicated tail of tokens from an earlier session. Happening ~5% of resumes. Attached pcap + original request/response headers.

maya (support): Thanks Alex — can you paste the sample headers + a small excerpt of the raw SSE frames you saw? Also which SDK and proxy (if any) are you using?

alex (customer): Using mobile SDK 1.4.3, traffic goes via our edge proxy (envoy). Here's a minimal excerpt from the capture (links below):

-- request headers --
GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Resume-Token: rT_abc123

-- server SSE frames (raw) --
data: {"id":"token-1","text":"...partial chunk"}

data: {"id":"token-2","text":"...more"}

data: [DONE]

(on resume)
data: {"id":"token-2","text":"...more"}

data: {"id":"token-3","text":"unexpected short tail"}

Seems like token-2 gets replayed but token-3 is truncated and then connection closes. pcap: https://files.example.com/pcaps/alex_resume.pcap

maya (support): Got it. We've seen similar-sounding issues but not with this exact pattern. I'm going to try to reproduce with a local proxy and the same resume token behavior. Raj — can you take a look at the pcap and try a repro on our staging runtime? Patch the request headers exactly (incl X-Resume-Token).

raj (support): Reproduced locally using a scripted reconnect that sends the same resume token. Repro steps:
1) Start a long-running stream: curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer test" "https://staging.api/streams?model=gpt-x"
2) Cancel mid-stream after ~12s (SIGINT). Capture resume token in response meta.
3) Reconnect with X-Resume-Token header. Observe server sends a couple frames from the previous session and then closes early.

I captured the server logs for the same timeline. Relevant snippet (from runtime logs):

[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] stream_id=stream-987 resume_token=rT_abc123 kv_cache_version=42 route=model-gpt-x-v1
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] stream_id=stream-987 resume_lookup=HIT token_map=kv:42 ttl_remaining=3600
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] route_switch_detected: route=model-gpt-x-v2 (fallback)
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] kv_cache_mismatch: expected=42 actual=43 -> serving_from_fallback_cache
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] emit_segment=token-2
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] emit_segment=token-3(partial)
[2026-03-15T12:01:34Z] stream_close(reason=kvcache_incompatibility)

Hypothesis: resume token maps into a KV cache namespace keyed by model variant + cache version. If the request gets routed to a different model variant (e.g., fallback to v2 due to capacity), the runtime attempted to serve using a different KV layout which produced a partial continuation and then closed the stream. That matches the duplicate token-2 and the truncated token-3.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Nice catch. This is different from the usual "missing final tokens" cases — it's a token -> kv namespace mismatch during resume. Things to note:
- Resume tokens currently encode a kv_cache_version + route id. If routing changes after token issuance (autoscaler/fallback), the token is still accepted but the runtime does a best-effort lookup which can map to a different backing store.
- If the backing kv layout differs (e.g., different key prefixes for attention cache or chunked segments), the resume loop can yield overlapping frames then encounter invalid chunk boundaries -> truncated segments.

Immediate mitigation we can push to staging today: when resume_token.route != selected_route, reject resume (HTTP 412) and force full restart; or, short-term, tighten resume TTL so tokens expire quicker on variant churn windows.

raj (support): I also noticed billing double-counts: each resume attempt in this flow increments a new stream meter while the initial partial frames are billed too. Billing-bot shows two separate stream ids for the same logical user request. Billing team, can you hold off charging until we confirm dedupe? @billing-bot tag included.

billing-bot: Noted — I'm flagging the two stream_ids (stream-987 and stream-988) to billing ops to evaluate dedup logic. Please provide the invoice/time windows if you want a formal review.

maya (support): For customer workaround: avoid resume from mobile SDK 1.4.3 (it reuses tokens aggressively). We can ship a hotfix: SDK 1.4.4 will validate route metadata before attempting resume and will fall back to a fresh stream if mismatch. Meanwhile, setting the edge proxy to route sticky to the same backend pool for short-lived streams reduces fallbacks.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Repro script we used (staging):

```
# repro.sh
# start stream
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer test" \
  "https://staging.api/streams?model=gpt-x" > out1.txt &
PID=$!
sleep 12
kill -INT $PID
# parse resume token from out1.txt (tooling extracts rT_*)
RESUME=$(grep -oP '"resume":"\K[^\"]+' out1.txt)
# reconnect with resume
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -H "X-Resume-Token: $RESUME" \
  "https://staging.api/streams?model=gpt-x" > out2.txt
```

Also tcpdump filter we used to collect the problematic corner case: `tcpdump -w resume_issue.pcap -s 0 '(tcp port 443) and host staging.api'`

ingrid (eng-runtime): Next eng steps:
- Disable best-effort resume when route != token.route (safety reject) — staging patch ready (PR #3412).
- Add additional logging: token->kv namespace id and a deterministic checksum of expected segment boundaries so we can reject on mismatch before emitting corrupted segments.
- Add unit tests for resume token mismatch across model variant swaps.

raj (support): I've attached the trimmed pcap and runtime logs to the ticket: https://tickets.redwood/cases/67890. Customer, can you confirm if you want us to roll the staging patch to production? We can do a rolling change with canary for 10% of resume traffic first.

alex (customer): Please do the canary. This is causing customer-facing truncation and odd duplicate tokens in logs, so a staged rollout sounds good. Thanks for the quick triage — also please keep me updated on billing dedupe.

maya (support): Will coordinate rollout + billing hold request. Closing initial triage here; moving this to eng-runtime for the patch. If anyone on the thread gets new captures, paste them in here. :thumbsup:
